name: Lower body lift

card.summary: A surgery that removes a circumferential band of loose skin and fat from the lower trunk after major weight loss, tightening the abdomen, flanks, buttocks and thighs.
card.note: Major surgery with a long scar and a significant complication profile; mainly for massive weight loss patients.

quick.overview:
A lower body lift, also called a belt lipectomy, is plastic surgery that removes loose skin and fat in a band around the lower trunk and lifts the tissue below it. It is mostly used after massive weight loss, when sagging skin on the abdomen, flanks, back, buttocks and outer thighs remains even though the weight is gone.

The appearance payoff is a tighter, more defined midsection and lower body that shows the results of the weight loss, sometimes with gluteal augmentation using the patient's own tissue. It is a staple of the body-contouring literature, with reviews, classification systems and complication studies behind it.
quick.how: A surgeon plans the incision line around the body, removes the skin and fat, and tightens the layers, often combining it with an abdominoplasty or thigh lift in stages. Patients are usually people who have reached and held a stable weight after dieting or bariatric surgery, and recovery takes weeks.
quick.risks: As major surgery it carries the risks of anaesthesia, wound-healing problems, fluid collections, infection, visible scarring and asymmetry; a prospective study has specifically examined complications after lower body lift in massive weight loss patients. Surgeons assess weight stability, health and smoking status before operating.

lead: A lower body lift, also known as a belt lipectomy, is a body-contouring operation that removes a circumferential band of skin and fat from the lower trunk and lifts the tissues of the abdomen, flanks, back, buttocks and often the outer thighs. It is most commonly performed after massive weight loss, when the skin has lost its ability to retract.[1][2]

People have it to change how their body looks after losing a large amount of weight: smoother contours, a tighter waist and abdomen, and a lifted lower body. Surgeons sometimes shape or augment the buttocks with tissue from the area being removed; one 2018 study proposed a classification and algorithm for gluteal augmentation in massive weight loss patients having a body lift.[3]

The procedure is covered in plastic-surgery reviews of body contouring, with comparative work on how skin differs after surgical versus diet-induced weight loss and a prospective study of complications.[1][4][5]

chain: Band of loose skin and fat removed around the lower trunk
Tighter abdomen, waist, buttocks and thighs
angle.text: The operation removes excess skin that diet and exercise cannot, so the contour from weight loss becomes visible. The trade-off is a long scar and a major recovery.

infobox: Abdomen, flanks, back, buttocks, outer thighs

paras: Body-contouring reviews describe a spectrum of operations for patients who have lost a lot of weight, including brachioplasty, upper body lift, abdominoplasty, lower body lift and thigh lift. Planning covers medical history, examination, a surgical plan and postoperative management, with attention to complications.[1] A 2023 review in Plastic and Reconstructive Surgery describes the contemporary lower body lift.[6]

Wikipedia's abdominoplasty article describes circumferential abdominoplasty, also called belt lipectomy or lower body lift, as removing excess tissue around the trunk, commonly after massive weight loss, to contour the abdomen, flanks and lower back.[9] Modern abdominoplasty was developed from the 1960s.[9]

Reviews of abdominal contouring in massive-weight-loss patients list panniculectomy, standard, fleur-de-lis and reverse abdominoplasty and circumferential variants such as the lower body lift, and the authors recommend limiting total body reconstruction to two stages with the abdomen in the first.[10] An oblique flankplasty is described as an alternative that narrows the waist and addresses the flank through an incision of different direction, with pros and cons compared with a lower body lift.[11]

The operation is mainly used by people with massive weight loss from diet or bariatric surgery, where sagging skin affects clothing fit, hygiene and body image. It is often discussed with abdominoplasty and other combined procedures, with the choice depending on where the excess tissue is.[2][7]

Thigh laxity after significant weight loss has vertical and horizontal components; one review says the vertical vector is best corrected first with a lower body lift or extended abdominoplasty, and the remaining medial thigh skin is then addressed separately.[12] Abdominoplasty is described as the fifth most common cosmetic plastic surgery procedure in the United States, and combining it with other operations, including lower back lift and thigh lift, has become the norm.[2]

A prospective comparative study examined histological differences in skin between morbidly obese patients after surgical and diet-induced weight loss, since skin elasticity can differ between the groups.[4]

Complications are a central topic. A prospective comparative study looked at complications after lower body lift in massive weight loss patients, and review articles list complications and pitfalls of body lifting alongside strategies to limit them.[1][5] The Wikipedia overview notes that changes after major weight loss occur gradually over years.[8]

Wikipedia lists complications of abdominoplasty including seroma, hematoma, infection, delayed wound healing, tissue necrosis, scarring, asymmetry and blood clots, with smoking, obesity, diabetes and combined procedures as risk factors, and says its complication rate is higher than many other cosmetic surgeries.[9] A 2008 study cited there examined seroma after contouring surgery for massive weight loss.[9]

Lower body lift is discussed in appearance communities as a step for people who have lost a lot of weight and are left with loose skin, usually alongside abdominoplasty and thigh lift. Practitioners describe it as the operation that lets the shape from weight loss show; patients and surgeons also weigh the long scar and staged recovery.

A 2013 prospective comparative study followed complications after lower body lift following massive weight loss.[5] A 2018 clinical study of body lifts proposed a gluteal augmentation classification and algorithm after a retrospective review of procedures performed from 2012 to 2017.[3] A 2012 clinical study compared skin histology after surgical and diet-induced weight loss.[4]

timeline.event: Modern abdominoplasty begins to be developed.[9]
Plastic and Reconstructive Surgery body-contouring review describes patient selection and the spectrum of lifts.[1]
A review of the lower-body lift appears in Aesthetic Surgery Journal.[7]
Prospective study of complications following lower body lift after massive weight loss published.[5]
Classification and algorithm for gluteal augmentation during lower body lift proposed.[3]
Contemporary Lower Body Lift review published.[6]

lore.intro: Body-lift surgery is mentioned in appearance communities as the surgical answer to loose skin after major weight loss.

claims.claim: Loose skin after major weight loss will not retract and needs surgery
claims.believers: Patients who have lost a large amount of weight report sagging skin remains despite diet and exercise.
claims.experts: Reviews describe body lifting for massive weight loss patients, and a prospective study compared skin histology after surgical versus diet-induced weight loss.[1][4]

claims.claim: A lower body lift also shapes the buttocks
claims.believers: Patients and surgeons describe lifting and, where wanted, augmenting the gluteal region in the same operation.
claims.experts: A 2018 retrospective review of body lifts from 2012 to 2017 proposed a classification and algorithm for gluteal augmentation.[3]

claims.claim: It trades loose skin for a long scar and a hard recovery
claims.believers: Patients accept a circumferential scar for the contour gain.
claims.experts: A prospective study examined complications after lower body lift, and reviews list pitfalls and ways to limit them.[1][5]

claims.claim: Staging and combining procedures gives a better overall result
claims.believers: Surgeons plan abdomen, flank and thigh work together.
claims.experts: Authors recommend limiting reconstruction to two stages with the abdomen first, and note that long combined operations raise risk.[2][10]
